summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.40/1804)

data.turoyo: <...> Fərṭiwo am mxaddat w məfqiwo i fərto w əxliwola. <...>
data.translation: <...> They would rip open the pillows and take out the bran and eat it. <...>

rationale: First active Infectum-wa; a complete coordinated sentence gives the purpose and material outcome of ripping open pillows. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; the sense is based on the Turoyo.
Makes explicit the reading already represented by inherited Detransitive examples 9/21–22; spontaneous garment damage, not a new lexical splitting meaning.

data.turoyo: me bəṯre dewo da knəflile ḥa, frəṭli gawe w qṭili.
data.translation: Einem der Wölfe verpasste ich eins mit dem Messer, schlitzte ihm den Bauch auf und tötete ihn.

rationale: Thin active Preterit cell; 1sg agent and zero-marked possessed belly patient, contrasting inherited plural fox agents.

summary: Restore Bale at the beginning of the quotation
rationale: The supplied verse 9/21 begins Bale kito hən mənayye. The entry has s in place of a in this word. This is a letter substitution, not a clitic-boundary, stress, or vowel-length convention.

summary: Active Preterit has an actor and a zero-marked body-part patient: first-person frəṭli gawe at 91/29 contrasts with fronted gawayye and overt l-agent lat taʕle at 91/59.

Detransitive 9/21 describes spontaneous deterioration of a garment; 9/22 describes its resulting damage. No external agent is entailed by either clause. These differ in participant coding from ripping open a belly, not in the core splitting meaning.
The reader's thin-cell flags at 9/21 and 9/22 refer to examples already present. Both are retained once; only the genuinely new 91/29 context is added.
Plural Fərṭiwo is coordinated with məfqiwo and əxliwola in a dearth narrative. The -wo series presents repeated actions; classify Infectum-wa rather than deriving a Preterit from English would.
The round-1 Detransitive sense 1 and its garment examples remain baseline. This active pillow-opening context does not add a Detransitive function.
9/21: is masculine-shaped kməfrəṭ with postverbal feminine dukṯo normal default agreement, or a transcription issue? Retain the source and inherited form pending verification.
Pillows replace the inherited body-part patients; the deliberate physical opening remains I.1. This is a participant extension, not a new sense or a Detransitive.
